title: FlowGate: composite-metric rollback triggers with per-cohort threshold tuning
creator: Ava Patel
description: Implement a production-ready composite rollback signal (FlowGate) that combines latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput into a single, tunable score for automated rollback decisions. FlowGate must support per-customer/cohort baselines, staged shadow validation, hysteresis (to avoid thrash), and safe defaults that require multi-window confirmation before any automated rollback. This ticket covers design, implementation, experiments, and rollout integration with the existing rollout controller and console alerts.
background: Current auto-rollback uses simple single-metric thresholds (latency or error-rate) and is noisy for bursty workloads and multi-tenant customers.

We need a multi-signal approach to reduce false positives while still surfacing real regressions. Token cost regressions and throughput degradations are important signals for platform economics and customer SLAs.
Design must integrate with canary, A/B, and shadow flows already in the rollout engine and provide per-route and per-customer tuning via the console.
acceptance_criteria: FlowGate score computed in runtime with configurable weights for latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput.
Per-cohort baseline subtraction: FlowGate computes delta from baseline for each customer/cohort.
Hysteresis rules applied: require 3 consecutive 1-minute windows OR a 5-minute aggregated window breach before automated rollback action is scheduled.
Shadow validation path: new model receives shadow traffic for 10% of requests for 48h and FlowGate deltas are recorded; System must show a dashboard of deltas.

Integration tests: rollout controller respects FlowGate decisions, and rollbacks are executed only after escalation policy (immediate for P0 customers disabled; manual approval for enterprise customers unless emergency flag set).
Simulated fault injections reproduce expected FlowGate decisions in test harness with >=90% precision/recall vs labeled incidents dataset.
Documentation and Console UI: knobs for weights, per-cohort baseline window, and rollback policies visible in rollout settings.
design_notes: FlowGate score = w1 * z(latency) + w2 * z(error_rate) + w3 * z(token_cost) - w4 * z(throughput) where z() = normalized delta from baseline (std-based).
Baseline windows: rolling 7d traffic baseline + 1h recent trend subtraction. Cohort baselines (account, region, route) computed asynchronously and cached in rollout engine.
Two-tier thresholds: soft threshold triggers alerting and increased sampling; hard threshold triggers automated rollback after hysteresis confirmation.
Shadow traffic strategy: compute per-request contribution to FlowGate for shadow model without affecting live responses. Use stateless collectors to avoid PII leakage.
Hysteresis and anti-thrash: introduce exponential backoff on repeated auto-rollbacks per deployment (cooldown period), and require manual review for >2 rollbacks within 24h on same model version.
A/B experiments: use control/cohort splits to validate false positive rates and tune weights via offline optimization (grid search then hill-climb).
Cost-sensitivity: token_cost normalized by request length distribution; include token cost per-token at model variant level.
progress_updates: 2025-11-18: Initial design doc reviewed with Reliability and Product; flagged requirement to surface per-account opt-out for auto-rollback for enterprise customers.
2025-11-21: Prototype of FlowGate score implemented in test harness (rust microservice) and validated against 50 labeled incidents — preliminary precision 0.88, recall 0.82.
2025-11-24: Implemented baseline service API and cached cohort baseline store; need to harden TTL eviction under high-cardinality accounts.
2025-11-29: Integrated hysteresis engine into rollout controller; manual rollback workflow wired into Console. Working on shadow validation dashboard charts.
Next: run canary-on-canary experiment for two weeks using internal traffic and prepare PR for runtime change.
risks: High-cardinality cohorts could make baseline computation expensive and increase memory footprint — mitigation: sample cohorts above threshold and fallback to route-level baselines.
Overfitting weights to historical incidents could miss novel failure modes — mitigation: keep conservative defaults and require manual approval for enterprise cohorts by default.
Token cost signal can be noisy for conversational workloads with variable length — mitigation: normalize by expected prompt/response length distribution and use percentiles instead of means.
Automated rollbacks might cascade across regions if routing policies are not independent — mitigation: per-region isolation and cascade guardrails in rollout controller.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): baseline service + FlowGate prototype in test harness; unit tests for scoring and normalization.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): integrate FlowGate into rollout controller, add hysteresis/rollback policy engine, and wire basic Console controls.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): shadow validation pipeline and dashboard; run internal canary experiments and tune weights.
Phase 4 (1 week): open beta for low-risk routes with opt-in per-team; monitor and iterate on thresholds.
Phase 5: enterprise rollout and enforcement knobs (per-customer opt-out, manual override playbooks).
testing_plan: Unit tests for score computation across synthetic distributions.
Integration tests that simulate canary traffic and verify controller decisions against expected outcomes.
Chaos tests: inject latency/error/cost regressions to ensure FlowGate flips and rollback executes only after hysteresis windows.
A/B validation: compare production outcomes with control using a 2-week A/B test on internal traffic.
playbook_notes: Automatic rollback triggers create an incident with auto-populated metrics and stack traces, assign to oncall for verification.
Manual override path in Console to pause auto-rollbacks for an account or model version.
Post-rollback checklist: collect sample requests, run evals against golden prompts, and open a postmortem if customer-impact > medium.
